the outcome of pancreatic surgery has improved over the last 15 years.
pancreatic resections are still associated with a considerable complication risk and that the outcome is still dependent on the surgeon’s experience and adequate perioperative management.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pancreatic resections can be performed with a very low mortality rate, and that pancreatic surgeons should focus on the prevention and treatment of pancreatic fistula.
pancreatic surgery can be performed with low mortality and acceptable morbidity even by less experienced pancreatic surgeons.
pancreatic surgery is safe, even in the hands of a few dedicated surgeons, and that a high volume is not necessarily required.
